newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar bounces after sell-off to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar bounces after sell-off to end firmer.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Friday as investors bought back into the currency after Thursday's sell-off, dealers said.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6903/08 and at 68.55 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from its 0.6885 and 68.30 opening levels.
"The Kiwi's had a relatively quiet day after the events of yesterday. It has recovered a touch from the open," said a chief bank dealer.
The Kiwi fell on Thursday after Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash's comments in an interview were interpreted as sanctioning an easing in monetary conditions.

Brash told a wire agency conditions were "still slightly stronger than we indicated as being desired on the 13th of March, and now...we're clearly in the process of looking at whether that line is still appropriate in preparing for our June Monetary Policy Statement".

Dealers said a combination of TWI-related buying, people who had sold on the news buying back, corporate interest out of New Zealand and interest to buy Kiwi against Aussie, had seen the currency recover from around 0.6885.

"I think the market's finally realised that the ongoing economic data we've been getting in the last month or so, together with (March quarter) CPI which was obviously on the softer side, gives the Reserve bank a great deal more comfort than perhaps we thought," the chief dealer said.
He said overall the Kiwi was headed lower.

"The market is looking for it to range trade now for the next week or so, but I don't think it's going to happen. I think the Kiwi is just biding time before it, I wouldn't say falls off a cliff, but before it comes under renewed selling pressure," he said.
The currency was seen trading a 0.6890-6925 range overnight.
